_meta.purpose: Labor cost lookup by geography x role, used by costEngine.ts for the labor baseline (volume x time x labor_cost). Cross-cutting across sector benchmark packs, not sector-specific.
_meta.no_silent_fallback: If geography is not IN, or role is not found for the given geography, the lookup must return null/not-found. costEngine.ts must not substitute an IN or any other rate silently - the field should surface as 'assumed' with a visible flag, or block until the user provides a value.
_meta.currency_note: All figures in INR (annual, fully-loaded is NOT implied by these figures - see notes per entry; most public salary data is base/total-cash pay, not employer fully-loaded cost including benefits/overhead. Fully-loaded multiplier applied in costEngine.ts, not baked in here - see _meta.fully_loaded_multiplier_todo).

fully_loaded_multiplier_todo: [TBD] - None of the sourced figures below are 'fully loaded cost' (they are cash comp as reported to salary aggregators). A standard India ITES/BPO fully-loaded multiplier (benefits, employer PF/ESI contributions, facilities, overhead) is commonly cited in the 1.3x-1.6x range in industry literature, but this spec has not sourced a specific citation for that multiplier yet. Do not hardcode a multiplier without a source - flag it as an assumed adjustment in the UI if applied.

source.name: Payscale - Average Customer Service Agent Salary in India

cross_check.name: Glassdoor - Customer Service Representative (India)
cross_check.note: Glassdoor's India dataset for this role reports ~INR 23,500/yr with an hourly figure (~INR 11/hr) that is internally consistent with an annual figure at 2080 hrs, but the resulting annual number is implausibly low for full-time work in India (below typical entry-level BPO pay). Likely a monthly-vs-annual labeling inconsistency in Glassdoor's scraped India data. Payscale figure used as primary for this reason - flagged here rather than silently discarding the discrepancy.

entries.notes: Cash comp, not fully-loaded. Represents entry-level/generalist support agent, most applicable to high-volume ticket-handling roles typical of the customer support automation sector pack.

Use for support roles requiring more technical/product knowledge than a generalist agent (e.g. escalation handling, tier-2 support) - distinct from IN-CS-AGENT-2026. City-level figures run notably higher (Bangalore/Mumbai/Chennai ~INR 6.5-6.8L median vs national INR 6.1L) - not included as separate entries yet, flagged as a possible future geography refinement below city level.

Glassdoor - Accounts Payable Clerk (India, national)
cross_check.note: Small sample (n=41) - treated as an upper-bound cross-check, not the primary figure, given low sample size relative to other sources.

entries.notes: ERI SalaryExpert figure used as primary median since its stated methodology (employer + employee survey data) is more transparent than Glassdoor's ML-predicted figures for this role, and it sits between the Indeed low and Glassdoor high rather than at either extreme.

Used for 'build' cost estimates in the buy-vs-build stage costing (section 6.4 of the spec) - this is engineering labor cost for building/integrating the AI solution itself, not the process being automated. Wide range reflects India's real experience-band spread (entry-level IT-services vs. product/FAANG comp) - the median is a national blended figure, not representative of any specific company tier. Treat 'high' as closer to product-company/specialist comp, 'low' as closer to IT-services-firm comp.
